items.informal_name: Weighted Total Degree is Preserved Under Injective Renaming of Variables
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] {σ : Type u_5} {τ : Type u_6} {e : σ → τ} {w : τ → ℕ} {P : MvPolynomial σ R},
  Function.Injective e →
    MvPolynomial.weightedTotalDegree w ((MvPolynomial.rename e) P) = MvPolynomial.weightedTotalDegree (w ∘ e) P
items.informal_description: For any injective function $ e : \sigma \to \tau $, weighting function $ w : \tau \to \mathbb{N} $, and multivariate polynomial $ P \in R[\sigma] $, the weighted total degree of the renamed polynomial $ \text{rename}(e, P) $ with respect to $ w $ equals the weighted total degree of $ P $ with respect to the composed weighting function $ w \circ e $. Formally, $ \text{weightedTotalDegree}_w(\text{rename}(e, P)) = \text{weightedTotalDegree}_{w \circ e}(P) $.

items.informal_name: Injective Dummy Variable Replacement in Diophantine Equations
items.type:
∀ {α β γ : Type u} {S : Set (α → ℕ)} (f : β → γ) (g : γ → Option β),
  (∀ (x : β), g (f x) = some x) →
    ∀ (p : Poly (α ⊕ β)),
      (∀ (v : α → ℕ), S v ↔ ∃ t, p (Sum.elim v t) = 0) → ∃ q, ∀ (v : α → ℕ), S v ↔ ∃ t, q (Sum.elim v t) = 0
items.informal_description: Given an injective function $f : \beta \to \gamma$ with partial inverse $g : \gamma \to \text{Option } \beta$ satisfying $g(f(x)) = \text{some } x$, and a polynomial $p$ in variables $\alpha \oplus \beta$ such that $S(v)$ holds iff there exists $t$ with $p(v \oplus t) = 0$, there exists a polynomial $q$ in variables $\alpha \oplus \gamma$ such that $S(v)$ holds iff there exists $t'$ with $q(v \oplus t') = 0$. This establishes equivalence preservation under injective variable substitution in Diophantine equations.

items.informal_name: Witt Structure Polynomial Compatibility with Renaming
items.type:
∀ (p : ℕ) {idx : Type u_2} [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {σ : Type u_3} (Φ : MvPolynomial idx ℤ) (f : idx → σ) (n : ℕ),
  wittStructureInt p ((MvPolynomial.rename f) Φ) n = (MvPolynomial.rename (Prod.map f id)) (wittStructureInt p Φ n)
items.informal_description: For any multivariate polynomial $\Phi$ over $\mathbb{Z}$ with variables indexed by $\text{idx}$, any function $f : \text{idx} \to \sigma$, and natural number $n$, applying the Witt structure polynomial construction to the renamed polynomial $\Phi$ (via $f$) at level $n$ is equivalent to renaming the variables in the Witt structure polynomial of $\Phi$ at level $n$ using the map $\text{Prod.map } f \, \text{id} : \text{idx} \times \mathbb{N} \to \sigma \times \mathbb{N}$. Formally, $\text{wittStructureInt}_p(\text{rename}_f(\Phi), n) = \text{rename}_{\text{Prod.map } f \, \text{id}}(\text{wittStructureInt}_p(\Phi, n))$.

items.informal_name: Injective Renaming Preserves Variable Degree in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] {p : MvPolynomial σ R} {f : σ → τ},
  Function.Injective f → ∀ (i : σ), MvPolynomial.degreeOf (f i) ((MvPolynomial.rename f) p) = MvPolynomial.degreeOf i p
items.informal_description: For any multivariate polynomial $ p $ over a commutative semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $, and for any injective function $ f : \sigma \to \tau $, the total degree of the variable $ f(i) $ in the renamed polynomial $ \operatorname{rename}(f, p) $ equals the total degree of the variable $ i $ in the original polynomial $ p $. Symbolically, $ \deg_{f(i)}(\operatorname{rename}(f, p)) = \deg_i(p) $.

items.informal_name: Injectivity Lemma for Polynomial Solutions with Dummy Variables
items.type:
∀ {α β γ : Type u} (f : β → γ) (g : γ → Option β),
  (∀ (x : β), g (f x) = some x) →
    ∀ (p : Poly (α ⊕ β)) (v : α → ℕ),
      (∃ t, p (Sum.elim v t) = 0) ↔ ∃ t, (Poly.map (Sum.elim Sum.inl (Sum.inr ∘ f)) p) (Sum.elim v t) = 0
items.informal_description: Given an injective function $ f : \beta \to \gamma $ with a partial inverse $ g : \gamma \to \text{Option } \beta $ satisfying $ g(f(x)) = \text{some } x $ for all $ x $, and a polynomial $ p $ in variables indexed by $ \alpha \oplus \beta $ with integer coefficients, the existence of a solution $ t $ such that $ p(v \otimes t) = 0 $ is equivalent to the existence of a solution $ t $ such that the substituted polynomial $ p.\text{map}(\text{inl} \oplus \text{inr} \circ f)(v \otimes t) = 0 $. This substitution preserves solvability under the injectivity condition.

items.type: {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_4} [CommSemiring R] {p : MvPolynomial σ R} {f : σ → τ} [DecidableEq τ] (h : Function.Injective f) : ((MvPolynomial.rename f) p).support = Finset.image (Finsupp.mapDomain f) p.support

∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_3} [inst : CommRing R] {τ : Type u_4} {S : Type u_5} [inst_1 : CommRing S]
  [inst_2 : Algebra R S] {a : σ → MvPowerSeries τ S} (w : τ → ℕ),
  MvPowerSeries.HasSubst a →
    (∀ (i : σ), a i ≠ 0) →
      ∀ (f : MvPowerSeries σ R),

items.informal_description: For any multivariate power series $ f $ over a commutative ring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $, and for any substitution $ a : \sigma \to \mathrm{MvPowerSeries}(\tau, S) $ satisfying the substitution condition and with each $ a(i) \neq 0 $, the weighted order of $ f $ with respect to the weight function $ \mathbb{N}^{\top} \to \mathbb{N} $ composed with the weighted orders of $ a(i) $ is less than or equal to the weighted order of the substituted power series $ f(a) $ with respect to the original weight function $ w $.

This holds because the zero polynomial is the only case where $ \text{weightedTotalDegree}' $ differs from the embedded $ \text{weightedTotalDegree} $.

  [inst_2 : Algebra R S] {a : σ → MvPowerSeries τ S} (w : τ → ℕ),
  MvPowerSeries.HasSubst a →
    ∀ (f : MvPowerSeries σ R),
      ⨅ d, ⨅ (_ : (MvPowerSeries.coeff d) f ≠ 0), (Finsupp.weight (MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder w ∘ a)) d ≤
        MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder w (MvPowerSeries.subst a f)
items.informal_description: For a multivariate power series $ f $ over a commutative ring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $, and a substitution map $ a: \sigma \to \mathrm{MvPowerSeries}(\tau, S) $ satisfying the substitution condition, the weighted order of the substituted series $ f[a] $ with respect to a weight function $ w: \tau \to \mathbb{N} $ is greater than or equal to the infimum of the weighted orders of the individual substitutions $ a(x) $ (composed with $ w $) over all non-zero coefficients of $ f $. Formally, $ \inf_{\substack{d \in \sigma \to_0 \mathbb{N} \\ \mathrm{coeff}_d(f) \neq 0}} \mathrm{weightedOrder}(w \circ a, d) \leq \mathrm{weightedOrder}(w, f[a]) $. This establishes a lower bound on the weighted order after substitution in terms of the substitution maps' weighted orders.

items.informal_name: Infimum over Image Set Equals Infimum over Original Set
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_4} [inst : CompleteLattice β] [inst_1 : DecidableEq α] {f : γ → α}
  {g : α → β} {s : Finset γ}, ⨅ x ∈ Finset.image f s, g x = ⨅ y ∈ s, g (f y)
items.informal_description: For any finite set $ s $ of type $ \gamma $, functions $ f : \gamma \to \alpha $ and $ g : \alpha \to \beta $, the infimum of $ g(x) $ over the image $ f(s) $ is equal to the infimum of $ g(f(y)) $ over the original set $ s $. Symbolically, $ \bigwedge_{x \in s.image\ f} g(x) = \bigwedge_{y \in s} g(f(y)) $.

items.informal_name: Infimum Equality: $\bigwedge_{b \in f(s)} g(b) = \bigwedge_{x \in s} g(f(x))$
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_4} [inst : SemilatticeInf α] [inst_1 : OrderTop α] [inst_2 : DecidableEq β]
  (s : Finset γ) (f : γ → β) (g : β → α), (Finset.image f s).inf g = s.inf (g ∘ f)
items.informal_description: Let $ s $ be a finite set of elements of type $ \gamma $, $ f : \gamma \to \beta $ a function, and $ g : \beta \to \alpha $ where $ \alpha $ is an infimum semilattice with a top element $ \top $, and $ \beta $ has decidable equality. Then, the infimum of $ g $ over the image of $ s $ under $ f $ is equal to the infimum of the composition $ g \circ f $ over $ s $. Formally, this is expressed as $ \bigwedge_{b \in f(s)} g(b) = \bigwedge_{x \in s} g(f(x)) $.

items.informal_name: Infimum Preservation under Image Composition for Finite Sets
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_4} [inst : SemilatticeInf α] [inst_1 : DecidableEq β] {s : Finset γ}
  {f : γ → β} (hs : (Finset.image f s).Nonempty) (g : β → α), (Finset.image f s).inf' hs g = s.inf' ⋯ (g ∘ f)
items.informal_description: For a non-empty finite set $ s $ over $ \gamma $, a function $ f : \gamma \to \beta $, and a function $ g : \beta \to \alpha $ where $ \alpha $ is an infimum semilattice and $ \beta $ has decidable equality, the infimum of $ g $ applied to the image $ f(s) $ equals the infimum of the composition $ g \circ f $ applied directly to $ s $. Formally, $ \inf_{b \in f(s)} g(b) = \inf_{c \in s} g(f(c)) $.

items.informal_name: Infimum of Composed Function Over Finite Set Equals Infimum Over Image
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_4} [inst : SemilatticeInf α] [inst_1 : DecidableEq β] {s : Finset γ}
  {f : γ → β} (hs : s.Nonempty) (g : β → α), s.inf' hs (g ∘ f) = (Finset.image f s).inf' ⋯ g
items.informal_description: For a non-empty finite set $ s $ of elements in $ γ $, a function $ f : γ → β $, and a function $ g : β → α $ where $ α $ is an infimum semilattice with top element, the infimum of the composition $ g ∘ f $ over $ s $ equals the infimum of $ g $ over the image $ f(s) $. Symbolically, $\inf_{x ∈ s} g(f(x)) = \inf_{y ∈ f(s)} g(y)$.

items.informal_name: Infimum Equality for Finite Sets in Complete Lattices
items.type: ∀ {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [inst : CompleteLattice β] (s : Finset α) (f : α → β), s.inf f = sInf (f '' ↑s)
items.informal_description: For any finite set $ s $ of type $ \alpha $ and function $ f : \alpha \to \beta $ where $ \beta $ is a complete lattice, the infimum of $ f $ over $ s $ (computed iteratively from the top element) equals the infimum of the image set $ f(s) $ in $ \beta $, i.e., $ \bigwedge_{b \in s} f(b) = \inf (f(s)) $.
